title: How to Apologize to Your Partner (With Examples) — cv.cm
description: How to apologize to your girlfriend or boyfriend: the parts of a real apology, example words for being late, forgetting, hurtful words or lying, and what to avoid.
h1: How do you apologize to your partner the right way?
answer: A real apology names what you did, shows you understand how it affected your partner, and takes responsibility without "but". Then say what you will do differently and ask what they need. Keep it short, do not make excuses or demand forgiveness, and let your changed behavior over the next weeks finish the apology.

body: Whether you are apologizing to a girlfriend, boyfriend, husband or wife, the parts of a good apology are the same. A study led by Roy Lewicki at Ohio State University tested six parts of an apology. Apologies with more parts were judged more effective. The most important part was acknowledging responsibility, and the second was offering to repair the damage. Asking for forgiveness mattered least.
In a relationship, that becomes five steps:

ol: Name what you did, specifically. "I forgot your birthday dinner" is better than "I'm sorry for everything".
Show you understand the impact. "You waited for me and felt like you weren't important to me."
Take responsibility, with no "but". "That was my fault."
Say what you will do differently, and make it concrete. "I've put all our important dates in my calendar with reminders."
Ask what they need. "Is there anything I can do to make this better?"

body.note: An apology is a start, not a ticket. Your partner will believe the words when your behavior over the next days and weeks matches them.

head: Situation
What you could say
rows: You were late again

"I'm sorry I was 40 minutes late tonight. You were waiting alone and that wasn't fair. It's the third time this month, so I can see why you're upset. From now on I'll leave earlier and message you if anything changes."
You forgot something important
"I'm really sorry I forgot our anniversary. I know it made you feel like I don't care, and I do. I've set reminders. Can I plan a proper evening this weekend?"
You said something hurtful in a fight

"What I said about your family last night was cruel, and I'm sorry. I was angry, but that's not an excuse. You didn't deserve that. I'm going to take a break next time instead of saying things like that."
You lied

"I lied to you about where I was on Friday. I'm sorry. I understand if it's hard to trust me right now. I'll answer any question you have honestly, and I know trust comes back through what I do, not what I say."
You ignored their messages
"I'm sorry I didn't reply all day. You were worried and I left you guessing. Next time I'm busy, I'll send a quick message to say so."
You embarrassed them in front of others
"I'm sorry for the joke I made at dinner. It embarrassed you in front of your friends. I won't make jokes about that again."

body: If you are apologizing by message, keep it short and offer to talk: "I'm sorry for what I said earlier. You didn't deserve that. Can I call you tonight?" Big apologies are usually better in person or on a call, where your tone is clear.

head: Mistake
Example
Why it fails
rows: Apology with an excuse
"I'm sorry, but I was really stressed."
The "but" cancels the apology. Explain later, if they ask.
Blaming their feelings
"I'm sorry you feel that way."
It says the problem is their reaction, not your action.
Gifts instead of words
Sending flowers with no conversation
A gift can be nice after an apology, not in place of one.
Demanding forgiveness
"I said sorry. Why are you still upset?"
Forgiveness takes time and is their choice.
Turning it around
"Well, you do it too."
It starts a new fight instead of ending this one.
Too long and all about you
Twenty minutes on how bad you feel
Your partner ends up comforting you.
Promising what you won't do
"I'll never be late again in my life."
A broken promise hurts more than a small, real one kept.

sections.h: How to calm an angry partner honestly
body: People search for how to calm a girlfriend who is angry (女朋友生气了怎么哄) or a boyfriend who is upset. The honest answer is that there is no trick. What works is the same for anyone:

ul: Ask before you guess. "I can see you're upset. Is it something I did?" Do not say "calm down"; it usually has the opposite effect.
Listen to the whole thing without defending. Nod, and summarize: "So you felt ignored when I stayed on my phone all evening."
If you did something wrong, apologize using the steps above.
Offer comfort in the way they like it. Some people want a hug, some want space, some want you to fix the problem. Ask: "Do you want me to help, or just listen?"
If they need time, give it, and say you are still there: "Okay, I'll give you some space. I'm here when you want to talk."
Do not try to buy the mood back with jokes, gifts or cute stickers while the problem is still unspoken. These work as repair after the talk, not instead of it.

body: If your partner is angry about something you did not do, you can still be kind: "I didn't mean to hurt you, and I'm sorry you had a bad night. Can we talk about what happened?" You do not need to confess to things you did not do.

sections.h: When your partner is not ready to forgive
body: After a serious hurt, such as a lie or cheating, one apology is not enough. Some things that help:

ul: Accept that they decide the pace. "I understand if you need time. I'm not going anywhere."
Do not keep apologizing every hour. It can feel like pressure. Show the change instead.
Answer their questions honestly, even uncomfortable ones.
Check in after a week or two: "How are you feeling about what happened? Is there anything else you need from me?"
Accept that they may decide to end the relationship. That is their right, and an apology does not oblige anyone to stay.

body: If the same hurt keeps happening, it is not an apology problem. It is a behavior problem. Apologizing again and again for the same thing, without changing, slowly destroys trust.

sections.h: When apologizing is not the answer
body: Apologies are for your own actions. If you find yourself always apologizing, even for things you did not do, just to stop your partner's anger or silence, that is a sign of an unhealthy pattern. Watch for:

ul: You apologize to avoid anger you are afraid of.
Your partner says your memory is wrong so often that you doubt yourself. See cv.cm's article on gaslighting.
Your partner never apologizes, but always demands apologies from you.

body: In these cases, it is not your fault, and you deserve support. cv.cm's codependency test can help you notice people-pleasing patterns.

body.note: If you feel afraid of your partner, contact local emergency services if you are in danger, or a domestic violence helpline. US examples are thehotline.org and loveisrespect.org; or contact a local service where you live.

faq.q: Should I apologize in person or by text?
faq.a: For anything serious, in person or on a call is better, because your tone and face show you mean it. A short text is fine to open the door: "I'm sorry. Can we talk tonight?"

faq.q: How do I apologize if my partner won't talk to me?
faq.a: Send one short, sincere message that names what you did and says you are ready to talk when they are. Then give them space instead of sending many messages.

faq.q: What do I say after "I'm sorry"?
faq.a: Say what you did, how you think it affected them, and what you will do differently. Then ask, "Is there anything you need from me?" and listen.

faq.q: Should I give a gift with an apology?
faq.a: Only after the words, and only if it fits your partner. A gift without a real apology can feel like you are trying to skip the hard part.

faq.q: Why does my partner say my apology isn't sincere?
faq.a: Often the apology included an excuse, focused on your feelings, or the same thing has happened before without change. Ask them what is missing, and listen to the answer.
